## Example 3.6 {#dc3-example-3-6 .dc-lesson .dc-proof}

<p>Prove the result for $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sin f(x))$ using the chain rule.</p>
<div class="dc-proof-layout"><div class="dc-proof-prompts"><p><strong>a)</strong> Let $y=\sin u$ where $u=f(x)$. Find $\dfrac{dy}{du}$ and $\dfrac{du}{dx}$:</p><p><strong>b)</strong> Apply the chain rule $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{dy}{du}\times\dfrac{du}{dx}$:</p><p><strong>c)</strong> By similar reasoning, we can establish the following:</p><p><span data-math="\frac{d}{dx}(\cos f(x))=\ldots"></span></p><p><span data-math="\frac{d}{dx}(\tan f(x))=\ldots"></span></p></div>
<div class="dc-proof-working dc-chain-proof fragment" data-fragment-index="0"><p><span data-math="\frac{dy}{du}=\cos u,\quad\frac{du}{dx}={\color{#b55224}f^{\prime}(x)}"></span></p><p><span data-math="\frac{dy}{dx}=\cos u\cdot{\color{#b55224}f^{\prime}(x)}"></span></p><p class="dc-final-rule"><span data-math="={\color{#b55224}f^{\prime}(x)}\cos f(x)"></span></p><p><span data-math="\frac{d}{dx}\cos f(x)=-{\color{#b55224}f^{\prime}(x)}\sin f(x)"></span></p><p><span data-math="\frac{d}{dx}\tan f(x)={\color{#b55224}f^{\prime}(x)}\sec^2 f(x)"></span></p></div></div><p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 21 · Example 3.6(a–c)</p>

::: notes
The argument f(x) remains intact; multiply by its derivative. Orange highlights the inner derivative, with proper superscript prime typography. All three completed results appear in one Next reveal, after working. Assume f is differentiable, angles in radians; the tangent rule holds where cos f(x) != 0. About three minutes.
:::
